instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The schema explicitly defines a Draft 2020-12 closed object envelope, fixes its schema identifier and artifact discriminator, requires the primary routing and payload fields, and delegates type-specific content to BrowserRecordingPayload.
atoms.title: Closed browser-recording artifact envelope

atoms.statement: created_at_utc is only a non-empty string, while projection_freshness, projection_health, and retention_class are unrestricted strings; the schema supplies no date-time format, enums, normalization, length limits, or compatibility rules for these required operational fields.
atoms.title: Required operational metadata lacks canonical domains

atoms.statement: Optional thread, node, provider-attempt, usage-event, producer, actor, detail, content, and source-surface references accept empty strings; receipt_refs permits empty and duplicate arrays, and routing_refs requires one non-empty entry but does not require uniqueness or define a resolver/consumer contract.
atoms.title: Correlation references are weakly constrained and ownerless

atoms.statement: InvocationProvenance is closed, requires invocation_source, enumerates user and automated sources, and conditionally requires agent_reason for agent_initiated, goal, prd, planning_wizard, and subagent invocations.
atoms.title: Automated invocations require a stated reason

atoms.statement: BrowserActionInput requires only action_type and has no if/then contracts tying each action to its required or forbidden operands; the optional input_action_label carries duplicate spellings and is not constrained to agree with action_type.
atoms.title: Action records permit operand-free and contradictory commands

atoms.statement: The action vocabulary includes click, type, fill_form, upload_file, and handle_dialog, and the input shape stores value, form_values, file_refs, and dialog_action, but no action-level authority, approval, consent, secret-handling, or redaction requirement is represented.
atoms.title: Sensitive and destructive inputs lack an authority boundary

atoms.statement: BrowserActionResult is a closed object with required provenance, success, timestamp, and redaction status, plus optional page, screenshot, PDF, console, network, warning, omission, and error references.
atoms.title: Action outcomes carry explicit success and redaction signals

atoms.statement: BrowserActionResult has no conditionals connecting success=false to error_code, redaction_status to omission or warning details, or redaction failure/blocking to suppression of page representations and artifact references; retryability, partial-output semantics, and rollback are unspecified.
atoms.title: Failure and redaction states do not govern exposed outputs

atoms.statement: PageRepresentation conditionally requires prompt_injection_chips and visible_card_ref when prompt_injection_detected is true, and requires identity, URL, detail level, and observation time for every representation.
atoms.title: Detected prompt injection requires visible warning data

atoms.statement: The prompt-injection conditional is one-way and prompt_injection_detected is optional; PageRepresentation also makes redaction_profile_id optional and has no invariant that governs sensitive representation references when detection or redaction is absent, false, or failed elsewhere.
atoms.title: Page safety and redaction provenance are optional

atoms.statement: BrowserRecordingPayload requires nested runtime_state and forces its discriminator to runtime_unavailable when top-level state is runtime_unavailable; it also requires fallback_route_ref when open_watch_state is fallback_open_external.
atoms.title: Unavailable and external-fallback states carry required support data

atoms.statement: The schema enforces top-level runtime_unavailable only in one direction and defines no compatibility matrix or transitions among state, nested runtime_state, open_watch_state, and show_when_possible; disabled_by_policy does not require the reason and remediation demanded for runtime_unavailable.
atoms.title: Independent state fields admit contradictory GUI truth

atoms.statement: Required actions and artifact_refs are arrays without minItems, maxItems, uniqueness, sequence numbers, causal links, batch status, or cleanup/rollback semantics; action results likewise expose no ordering or concurrency identity beyond their timestamps.
atoms.title: Recording sequences lack ordering, concurrency, and scale bounds

atoms.statement: The schema exposes accessibility, layout, content, screenshot, PDF, console, network, runtime, and remediation references but names no resolving consumers or ownership boundary; URL and timestamp strings have no formats, reference strings lack canonical identifier constraints, and no localization, accessibility outcome, support telemetry, or executable cross-reference oracle is specified.
atoms.title: Consumer semantics and executable acceptance oracles are absent

cross_document_questions: Which canonical contract owns reference resolution, authorization, retention, and deletion for recording_ref, artifact_refs, page representation refs, receipt refs, and routing refs?
Which GUI contract defines the compatibility matrix among payload state, runtime_state, open_watch_state, show_when_possible, prompt-injection warnings, and redaction outcomes?
Which executor contract defines required operands, authority checks, ordering, concurrency, retry, cancellation, and rollback for every BrowserActionInput action_type?
